meta.title: Frely CLI — Your AI, connected to your computer
meta.description: Use ChatGPT or Claude Code on another computer to read files, run commands and manage processes on your own machine. Connect through Frely device MCP with OAuth.
meta.socialDescription: Your AI, connected to your computer. One device MCP service for ChatGPT, Claude Code and other remote MCP clients.
hero.description: Use ChatGPT in your browser or Claude Code on another computer to work with your files, run commands and manage processes. Frely CLI connects the computer you control as a device MCP service.
principles.label: Project highlights
workflows.description: Start with device MCP. Local model sharing has a separate setup; remote Agent integration follows its own release availability.
workflows.label: Device MCP and other CLI tools
tools.summary: Your computer, available to your AI clients.

tools.label: DEVICE MCP / CONNECT A CLIENT
tools.description: The same device MCP service accepts ChatGPT, Claude Code on another computer, and other remote HTTP MCP clients with OAuth. Commands run on the controlled computer.
tools.note: Clients of one device share its workspace and managed processes. File tools respect the workspace; shell commands run with the device OS account’s permissions, without a workspace sandbox.
agents.label: REMOTE AGENTS / IN DEVELOPMENT
agents.description: Remote Agent integration is in development. The npm release verified for this page, 0.6.1, lacks Agent install and invoke commands.
agents.note: The planned flow preserves your host’s model provider configuration and invokes a hosted Frely Agent. Installation instructions require a verified supporting release.
models.label: LOCAL MODELS / PROVIDERS
models.description: Connect a running Ollama or another loopback OpenAI-compatible runtime as a personal Frely Provider. Use it through your existing Frely Access Points and API keys.
models.note: Requires a running local model and an empty, active personal Provider slot. Local MCP execution requires separate authorization.
install.description: After installation, run these commands on the computer you want to control. Start in the folder you want your AI to use.
source.description: Frely CLI and this page are open source. Explore the code, report an issue, or contribute a change.
source.note: The CLI connects to Frely’s hosted Relay service. The open-source client and local MCP runtime are licensed under Apache-2.0; use of Frely trademarks is subject to the trademark policy.
footer.note: Your AI, connected to your computer
copy.failure: Copy unavailable. The command is selected; use your device’s copy action.
tools.prepare: Run these commands in the folder on the computer you want to control. Approve the device and workspace in your browser. Keep that computer running and online.
tools.connect: Use the complete address from frely mcp url. Each calling client signs in with your Frely account through OAuth; the address contains no access token.
tools.verify: Ask the client to use the Frely workspace_info and list_directory tools. Check that the returned folder and names match the controlled computer. The client’s built-in shell still operates on the calling computer.
tools.diagnostics: Use frely doctor for configuration and connection status, or frely doctor -v for detailed diagnostics. A real tool result verifies the client-to-device connection.
models.verify: Send a request to the selected model through a Frely Access Point with its API key. Use the model’s reply to verify inference; the Provider list records registration status.
install.diagnostics: Need to check the connection? Run frely doctor on the controlled computer. Add -v for detailed diagnostics.
install.next: Add this address to your client, choose OAuth, and authorize access. Keep the controlled computer running and online.
tools.chatgpt: Add a remote MCP connection with your device URL, select OAuth, and authorize with your Frely account. The same URL works for other compatible clients.
tools.claudePrepare: On the calling computer, replace <MCP_URL> with the address from the controlled computer. Give each device a different server name.
tools.claudeAuthorize: Open /mcp in Claude Code to finish OAuth authorization. Ask it to use the Frely tools for work on the remote computer. Frely CLI is only required on the controlled computer.
install.approval: Approve the device, workspace and duration in your browser. Frely CLI starts a background service.
device.description: Choose the AI client that fits your work. Frely routes its tool calls to the computer you authorized and returns the results.
device.browserTitle: ChatGPT, with your files and tools.
device.browserDescription: Connect your device MCP URL in ChatGPT. Ask it to inspect a project, edit files or run a command on your computer.
device.browserExample: “Read this project’s README and summarize how to run it.”
device.computerTitle: Claude Code, working on your other machine.
device.computerDescription: Connect Claude Code on your laptop to Frely CLI on your workstation. Use the workstation’s files and command-line tools through MCP.
device.computerExample: “Use the Frely tools to check the build on my workstation.”
device.targetTitle: Execution stays on the computer you connect.
device.targetDescription: Files · Shell commands · Managed processes. Your device connects out to Frely; no public listening port or router configuration is needed.
device.compatibility: Requires a remote HTTP MCP client with OAuth support. Device permission and client authorization are separate. Keep the controlled computer running and online.
